content.title: Labeled snapshots, not an SLA
content.lede: The current generic CLI is faster than wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 at every tested report size. The 0.2.6 perf-time work cut warm 500-page time from 1,228.72 ms to a measured 576.33 ms (2.13x) at 163.03 MB B/op, 30.6% below the 234.92 MB ceiling, and the phase-6 capture of that same code met the 615 ms stretch target. The closure re-capture 15 minutes later measured 733.48 ms at 500 pages in a slower host window with identical B/op, so both rows are labeled. Image rows are 1.97x / 2.22x faster with lossless PNGs about 50% larger. The concurrent-layout prototype was rejected (5.4% paired gain against a 15% floor) and left unwired. Open the Benchmarks page for the visual comparison.

content.title: Allocation targets met; time targets split across two labeled windows
content.body: The perf-time closure capture holds every allocation target: 500-page B/op is 163.02 MB (warm matrix), 167.87 MB (standalone), and 169.65 MB (public library), 28.4% to 30.6% below the pre-time baselines and under the 234.92 MB ceiling. The 500-tile image time holds at 44.27 ms. The warm 500-page time did not reproduce the phase-6 result in this closure window: 733.48 ms matrix median and 695.42 ms standalone, with identical B/op. The phase-6 capture of the same production source measured 576.33 ms / 163,032,880 B, a 2.13x speedup that met the 615 ms stretch target, and the plan's measured-lever floor (<= 830 ms) holds in the closure capture. The 250-tile image median is 25.72 ms, 0.72 ms above the 25 ms line; the phase-5b raw samples measured 24.15 ms. Raw evidence: plans/0.2.6/perf-time/results/phase-7/final-capture.md.

content.title: Lossless PNGs about 50% larger, an intended trade
content.body: The image rows are 1.97x / 2.22x faster than the pre-time baselines while the encoded PNG grows from 94,352 to 141,917 bytes at 250 tiles and from 188,268 to 282,749 bytes at 500 tiles. The filter-none level-2 streaming writer (internal/imageout/pngfast.go) replaced image/png adaptive filtering above the direct-raster threshold. PNG stays lossless, decoded pixels are bit-identical, and files stay far below the 32 MiB maxImageEncoded budget.

content.title: Concurrent-layout prototype rejected, left unwired
content.body: The phase-6 prototype rendered independent top-level sections in parallel and merged deterministically. It passed the equivalence contract (op-for-op display lists, page counts, date-normalized PDF bytes, golden 65/65, flat B/op), but its best paired same-process gain was 5.4% (serial 596 ms versus 564 ms at W=2), below the required 15% floor. It was rejected for shipping, pipeline overlap was not attempted, and production stays serial. The prototype and its differential tests were deleted in the 0.2.6 cleanup (plans/0.2.6/ponytail/0.2.6-ponytail-audit.md); no production caller remains.

content.title: Generic CLI, not the island-era path
content.body: The 2026-09-11 CLI comparison rows are the generic convert path against wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 with patched Qt, from the dated recovery capture; the perf-time capture measured gowkhtmltopdf only in cli-rss mode. The current in-process and library engine rows are three independent 1x samples per workload from the perf-time closure capture, one fresh process each; the reported value is the median of the three raw samples and B/op is never averaged. 2-page B/op includes the one-time default-font work (about 4.0 MB on the internal path), so it is not like-for-like with the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix. Median of three timed process runs after one warmup for the CLI cells. Peak RSS is /usr/bin/time %M and is never mixed with B/op. Do not compare these RSS numbers to older island-era CLI snapshots.

content.heading: Historical public library PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
Historical in-process PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
What the numbers mean
items: CLI comparison is process wall time plus peak RSS for freshly built gowkhtmltopdf versus the installed wkhtmltopdf binary.

The current CLI comparison matrix comes from the dated 2026-09-11 recovery capture on the uncommitted 0.2.6 working tree (VERSION 0.2.5); the current engine rows come from the 2026-09-11 perf-time phase-7 closure capture on the same tree, which measured gowkhtmltopdf only. The in-process and library rows are three independent 1x samples per workload; the published value is the median of the three raw values and B/op is never averaged.

The perf-time closure window ran slower on wall time than the phase-6 capture 15 minutes earlier (733.48 ms versus 576.33 ms at 500 pages) with identical production source hashes and identical B/op. The 2.13x result is the phase-6 row; the closure rows are kept alongside it rather than replaced.
The image rows trade about 50% more lossless PNG bytes for roughly 2x faster encoding; decoded pixels and dimensions are unchanged.
The concurrent-layout prototype (5.4% paired gain against a 15% floor) is rejected for shipping and has no production caller.

2-page B/op rows include the one-time default-font work (about 4.0 MB on the internal path) because each sample is a fresh 1x process. Do not compare them to the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix without that caveat.

The public Go library rows call Document.WritePDF and ImageDocument.WriteImage directly. The approximately 20x landing claim keeps the dated recovery-capture boundary: 258 ms divided by 10.88 ms at 2 pages, using the wkhtmltopdf CLI as the baseline.

The report fixture is testdata/golden/benchmarks/templates/report.html.tmpl with 20 invoice rows per requested page. Page islands and their convert.NewBenchmarkPDFRequest opt-in were removed in the 0.2.6 cleanup; every row is a generic-path measurement.
Full matrices, historical snapshots, and raw go test rows live in testdata/golden/benchmarks/, documentation/performance.md, and plans/0.2.6/perf-time/results/phase-7/.
